Exposure-response estimate with a bootstrap sensitivity interval

Source: R/pollution.R
exposure_response_plr.Rd

Fits the partially linear exposure-response model with plr_crossfit (or any estimator with the same interface), then re-fits it on n_bootstrap non-parametric resamples of the rows for a percentile interval (Efron and Tibshirani 1993, chapter 13).

Usage

exposure_response_plr(
  data,
  outcome,
  exposure,
  confounders,
  n_bootstrap = 100L,
  random_state = 42L,
  estimator = plr_crossfit
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

outcome, exposure, confounders

Column names.

n_bootstrap

Number of resamples (default 100).

random_state

Seed for the resampling.

estimator

A function (data, outcome, treatment, covariates) returning a list with ate and se. The default is plr_crossfit; rmorie's morie_estimate_double_ml() has the same interface.

Value

A list with ate, se_analytic, se_bootstrap, ci_lower_bs, ci_upper_bs, n_bootstrap and method.

References

Efron, B. and Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). An Introduction to the Bootstrap. Chapman and Hall.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(200), x2 = rnorm(200))
d$exposure <- 20 + 2 * d$x1 + rnorm(200)
d$asthma <- 5 + 0.3 * d$exposure + d$x2 + rnorm(200)
exposure_response_plr(d, outcome = "asthma", exposure = "exposure",
                      confounders = c("x1", "x2"), n_bootstrap = 20)$ate
#> [1] 0.2536464
